Daily Brief

Diplomatic momentum on Ukraine accelerated Friday as the Kremlin announced trilateral peace talks with the US and Ukraine are scheduled for early November in Abu Dhabi [The Hindu, BBC], though Kyiv reported continued Starlink connectivity issues affecting drone operations despite President Trump's claims that restrictions had been lifted [BBC]. Oil markets spiked to $114 per barrel amid reports the Trump administration is considering renewed strikes on Iran after the midterms [RNZ, Financial Times], while tech stocks suffered a significant sell-off on mounting concerns over AI-sector debt sustainability [Nikkei, Financial Times]. In France, authorities extended Paris curfews and banned protests in Lyon and Marseille ahead of expected weekend demonstrations, with President Macron labeling unauthorized protests 'illegitimate' following last weekend's widespread unrest [BBC, RFI]. West Africa faced a public health crisis as Nigeria confirmed an Ebola case in Abuja linked to travel from Congo, expanding an outbreak that has already reached Kenya [The Guardian]. Meanwhile, a BBC investigation documented 43 attacks on hospitals by Sudan's RSF during the siege of el-Fasher, with the UN human rights chief calling the findings evidence of potential war crimes [BBC].

Russia-Ukraine-US Peace Talks Scheduled for November in Abu Dhabi

  • Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov announced trilateral talks between Russia, Ukraine and the US are planned for early November in Abu Dhabi in a three-party format
  • The announcement followed meetings between US special envoy Steve Witkoff and both President Zelensky in Oslo and President Putin in St. Petersburg this week
  • Putin stated talks would focus on security arrangements for a final peace deal rather than a short truce; Russia suggested around November 10 as a target date
  • Ukraine called for discussions to happen 'as soon as possible' while both sides voiced readiness to resume direct talks mediated by Washington

  • Ukrainian defense ministry sources told the BBC that drones continue experiencing connection loss at speeds exceeding 161km/h (100mph), hampering military operations

05 Conflict

BBC Investigation Documents Systematic RSF Attacks on Hospitals in Sudan's El-Fasher

  • BBC documented at least 43 separate attacks on hospitals and healthcare sites in el-Fasher from May 2024 to October 2025, some facilities hit multiple times
  • From April 2023 to October 2025, 120 medical workers were injured, 55 killed, and 10 forcibly disappeared or abducted
  • UN human rights chief Volker Türk called findings 'deeply disturbing,' stating attacks may amount to war crimes under international humanitarian law
  • RSF rejected the findings; the health minister of RSF's civilian-affiliated government dismissed allegations as propaganda to smear their reputation
